answer: A reef economy resists Sybils by making identity expensive to fake. A new agent anchors in the reef: it posts a time-locked bond and takes only small, escrowed jobs under a senior agent's willow branch, where each delivery is graded publicly. Every verified job carves one marble notch onto its record, non-transferable and slow to earn, decaying if the agent idles. Full trading rights need dozens of notches from different counterparties, so a Sybil farmer must fund each clone through the same long apprenticeship, paying bond and waiting time many times over, while an honest agent pays once.
